shipFamilies.fleetUse: Local security, interception and close escort with low deployment burden.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Limited stores and lighter citadel make prolonged remote pursuit and concentrated heavy fire inefficient.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: Sustained patrol, escort and reconnaissance around formal trade and security corridors.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Higher crew and service burden than a corvette; isolated patrols are vulnerable when denied repair access.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: Layered fleet screen and strike-defense element protecting more valuable capital units.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Mass spent on redundancy and screening lowers independent offensive efficiency and raises replacement cost.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: Independent command combatant and durable center of medium task groups.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Capital-heavy procurement and conspicuous signature make unsupported deep projection expensive and observable.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: Prepared-system line firepower and protected strategic fleet anchor.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Exceptional capital, yard, crew and replenishment burden; route and yard loss can strand surviving hull value.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: Protected aviation and small-craft projection inside a supported fleet ecosystem.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Low direct line efficiency and strong dependence on escorts, stores, repair and replenishment infrastructure.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: State and market bulk cargo movement supporting arsenals, yards and reserve nodes.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Conservative protection consumes payload mass; throughput falls sharply when convoy routes are stretched.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: Finite reaction-mass and stores replenishment for deployed fleet groups.
shipFamilies.counterplay: High-value logistics target whose loss constrains remote acceleration and return endurance without applying a hidden debuff.

shipFamilies.fleetUse: Mobile repair, recovery and salvage work extending the value of expensive Imperial hulls.
shipFamilies.counterplay: Service machinery and stores displace combat systems; loss of these ships converts survivable damage into strategic downtime.

stations.visualBrief: Armored axial arsenal with recessed magazines, protected transfer galleries, graphite structure, ivory service blocks and restrained burgundy navigation marks.
Massive repairable yard complex with old structural frames, heavy service gantries, protected berths, replaceable modern equipment blocks and sparse brass authority plates.
Protected command and precision-industry hub: layered central citadel, redundant sensor masts, strict rectangular service geometry and minimal ceremonial state marking.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Measured legal language, formal obligations and documented procedure.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Protective of institutional continuity and quietly skeptical of improvised political shortcuts.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Short naval orders, readiness language and explicit responsibility.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Values preservation of trained crews and repairable capital assets over theatrical victories.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Precise cargo, route, reserve and delivery terminology.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Pragmatic about market access and deeply concerned by fragile long-distance supply promises.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Maintenance windows, work orders, tolerances and parts availability.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Proud of keeping decades-old hulls useful and hostile to unserviceable prestige engineering.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Evidence-qualified reports with provenance and confidence limits.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Suspicious of claims that outrun observed data even when senior officials want certainty.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Polite paternal administrative language and local patronage obligations.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Worried that distant central commitments can become expensive promises frontier systems must physically sustain.

missions.semanticIntent: Move finite reserve cargo into a lawful arsenal or yard buffer before a readiness deadline.
Procure and physically deliver ordnance inputs through ordinary market and freight paths.
Escort a real logistics convoy to its destination without substituting abstract convoy success.
Restore finite reaction-mass readiness of a named stranded fleet through physical replenishment.
Obtain owner-local discovery evidence for a strategically relevant object or system.
Recover finite salvage from a discovered derelict for ordinary industrial reuse.
Bring a real Stage-21E defensive operation to its requested terminal state around a threatened corridor.
Deliver finite repair or construction inputs to an ordinary project rather than grant repair progress.
Resolve a formal access problem through existing treaty and legal-market authority.
Assemble a named persistent fleet at the designated staging system through ordinary movement orders.

storyChains.semanticIntent: Formal access creates a lawful supply obligation that must be fulfilled by real cargo and protected traffic.
Observed threat leads to real defensive operations and finite reconstruction work rather than scripted restoration.

visualRules.requirement: Without color or heraldry the silhouette must read as protected prow, heavier central citadel, segmented serviceable armor and dense engineering stern; no fantasy wings or ornamental fins.
Graphite and gunmetal dominate, warm ivory is secondary, burgundy is restrained, brass marks authority only, and emissive cyan/amber/red remain functional.
Every character composes the shared hand-painted ink-and-gouache Character Master with the Empire faction overlay, role brief and individual brief.
Rank is readable through cut, material quality, cleanliness and restrained insignia rather than costume-like historical imitation or excessive decoration.
Old structures may carry newer electronics and replacement panels; wear communicates long maintained service, never abandonment or random greeble noise.
